metadata.note: The Utah and Northern Railway, researched from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites in response to a question about whether Idaho Falls, ID ever had passenger rail service -- it did, and this dataset had no coverage of it at all before (the existing Oregon Short Line file runs east-west through Pocatello, a separate corridor well south of Idaho Falls). Built north from Brigham City, UT starting in 1871 as a money-saving 3-foot narrow gauge, the line reached Eagle Rock (renamed Idaho Falls in 1891) in 1879 and Butte, MT by the end of 1881, giving Idaho Falls its first rail connection. After an 1887 standard-gauge conversion, the line passed through the Oregon Short Line & Utah Northern Railway (1889) into Union Pacific control (1898), and carried UP's Salt Lake City-Butte flagship, the Butte Special, from 1921 until Amtrak's 1971 formation, which did not retain the route -- no passenger train has run it since. Route geometry follows the real intermediate towns the line's own history describes, but is a simplified handful of waypoints, not surveyed track centerline. Era boundaries follow real corporate-history milestones (line openings, gauge conversion, mergers, the named train's launch and end); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not sourced from real timetables.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Construction began at Brigham City, UT in Aug 1871; laid as 3-foot narrow gauge to save money, Utah & Northern rails didn't cross into Idaho until May 1874. Regular trains reached Eagle Rock (renamed Idaho Falls in 1891), 210 miles north of Ogden, Apr 15 1879 (shown here for the full route regardless). estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
